artworks.title: River gods consoling Peneus for the Loss of his Daughter, Daphne
artworks.artist: Master of the Die (after Baldassare Peruzzi)
artworks.description: This Metropolitan Museum engraving (inv. 49.97.326) makes Peneus the mourner at the centre: fellow river-gods gather to console the Thessalian father after Daphne becomes the laurel. Designed after Peruzzi and cut by the Master of the Die, the print is among the clearest Renaissance images of the river-god himself, not only of Apollo's chase.

artworks.title: Daphne embracing her father, the river-god Peneus
artworks.artist: Master of the Die (after Baldassare Peruzzi)
artworks.description: Another plate from the same Met series shows Daphne clinging to Peneus as nymphs bring jars — Ovid's moment when the daughter begs her river-father to change her form before Apollo arrives. The Thessalian Potamos is named and staged as the parental power behind the laurel.

artworks.title: Daphne consulting her father
artworks.artist: Master of the Die (Bernardo Daddi attribution on plate)
artworks.description: Daphne kneels before the enthroned river-god — Peneus as the father who yields her wish for perpetual virginity before the pursuit begins. Early-modern print culture made this consultation a fixed beat of the Apollo and Daphne cycle.

artworks.title: Apollo in Love with Daphne
artworks.description: Poussin's unfinished Louvre canvas gathers the Ovidian episode into a classical landscape: Apollo pursues, Daphne flees toward her river-father, and the metamorphosis begins at the grove's edge. Peneus is the paternal shore toward which the nymph runs.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Book 1 makes Peneus the Thessalian father who answers Daphne's prayer and turns her into the laurel — the river-god as the hinge of Apollo's most famous metamorphosis.

popCulture.title: Pineios (Thessaly)
popCulture.description: The Thessalian river still bears the god's name — Peneus as living geography under Mount Olympus and the vale of Tempe.
